decision: Partitioned for fpga_prototype as an FPGA-oriented transport-and-safety wrapper around an external CPU/GPU software surrogate service. The DoMINO surrogate remains in GPU/CPU software because the qualification run did not prove hardware-deployable inference. Hardware handles deterministic control supervision, validation, timeout handling, command clamping, and safe fallback; software handles STL geometry packaging, reference evaluation, surrogate execution, and optimization/validation analysis.
decision_factors: Selected model nvidia.domino.automotive_aero is provisionally compatible but not accuracy-qualified and explicitly requires a GPU worker/remote NIM runtime.
No evidence was provided that the surrogate is hardware-deployable, so it remains in GPU/CPU software.
The architecture specifies an FPGA-first control wrapper that does not implement the surrogate, only transport, validation, clamping, and fallback.
Acceptance gates require deterministic command bounding, stale-data rejection, timeout handling, and safe fallback, which are best enforced in FPGA logic.
Transparent reference computation is required for 100% of validation cases and is explicitly suited to CPU software for traceability.
STL geometry ingestion and DrivAerML-compatible packaging are software tasks due to parsing and host-memory handling needs.
Interface constraints favor compact register/packet protocols rather than large geometry tensors on hardware pins.
The implementation path is fpga_prototype, but the contract does not bind to a board or specific fabric.
Safety requirements mandate fault latching, safe default behavior, and independent fallback availability, which favors hardware enforcement of the last-mile control path.
Architecture optimization and validation traceability are design-time software activities rather than real-time hardware datapath functions.

interfaces.name: geometry_input
interfaces.rationale: STL handling requires parsing and host-side file/memory access.
interfaces.responsibility: Accept STL geometry input and provide validated geometry for reference and surrogate evaluation.

interfaces.name: operating_condition_input
interfaces.rationale: Input acquisition and range normalization are host orchestration tasks.
interfaces.responsibility: Provide normalized stream-velocity values within 20-55 m/s to the control pipeline.

interfaces.name: reference_output
interfaces.rationale: The reference path is required to be transparent and traceable.
interfaces.responsibility: Deliver transparent baseline outputs for validation and comparison.

interfaces.name: control_command_output
interfaces.rationale: Actuator command generation and clamping are deterministic safety functions assigned to hardware.
interfaces.responsibility: Emit bounded actuator commands only after validity, freshness, and timeout checks pass.

interfaces.name: safety_status_output
interfaces.rationale: Host integration requires explicit observability from the hardware supervisor.
interfaces.responsibility: Report fault, freshness, timeout, clamp, and fallback states to the host control stack.

interfaces.name: fallback_control_interface
interfaces.rationale: Safe fallback must be available independently of model output validity.
interfaces.responsibility: Assert safe hold or predefined safe actuator state when validity cannot be guaranteed.

interfaces.name: validation_telemetry
interfaces.rationale: Logging, audit, and test evidence collection are software-centric and should not burden the real-time path.
interfaces.responsibility: Collect logs and evidence for traceability, acceptance gating, and performance validation across the operating envelope.

interfaces.name: compact_model_request_payload
interfaces.rationale: The architecture intentionally avoids exposing bulk geometry on top-level FPGA ports.
interfaces.responsibility: Carry compact request metadata such as sequence ID, flow-condition encoding, geometry token, operating-point ID, and control flags.

interfaces.name: compact_model_response_payload
interfaces.rationale: Response validation relies on a compact, bounded protocol between FPGA supervision and the external service.
interfaces.responsibility: Return compact response metadata including sequence ID, validity, predicted metrics, and service status.

jobs.latency_budget: offline or pre-cycle; must complete before control-cycle request issuance
jobs.rationale: Geometry parsing and STL handling are not hardware-deployable in the provided architecture and are better kept in software with direct access to host-managed memory and file I/O.
jobs.responsibility: Parse and validate STL geometry derived from DrivAerML reference geometry, perform structural readiness checks, and package a compact geometry descriptor or host pointer token for downstream use.

jobs.latency_budget: per evaluation/control cycle; sub-cycle on host side
jobs.rationale: Condition ingestion is a host/software concern because it is closely tied to orchestration, envelope validation, and request packaging.
jobs.responsibility: Receive, normalize, and range-check stream velocity inputs across 20-55 m/s and convert them into compact operating-point encodings for the control path.

jobs.latency_budget: validation-time / offline or nearline; must cover 100% of validation cases
jobs.rationale: The architecture explicitly assigns the transparent reference path to CPU software for traceability and validation. This path must remain observable and easy to audit.
jobs.responsibility: Compute the transparent baseline aerodynamic response/control estimate for every validation case and serve as the traceable reference path.

jobs.latency_budget: bounded by control timeout threshold configured in hardware; service must respond within the programmable timeout
jobs.rationale: The selected model requires a GPU worker and remote NIM-style runtime; no evidence supports hardware deployment, so it stays in GPU/CPU software.
jobs.responsibility: Execute the physics-based DoMINO surrogate in a remote GPU/CPU service using the compact request/response contract, without assuming RTL implementation.

jobs.latency_budget: per control cycle; must produce inputs before hardware commit deadline
jobs.rationale: High-level partitioning and policy assembly are best handled in software, while hardware enforces deterministic safety constraints.
jobs.responsibility: Separate estimation, decision logic, command shaping, validity checking, and safety supervision into explicit software responsibilities and generate compact control intent for hardware enforcement.

jobs.latency_budget: single control-cycle latency; deterministic and bounded
jobs.rationale: This is the core real-time safety function explicitly mapped to FPGA in the architecture, with small FSM, clamp logic, and command packing.
jobs.responsibility: Clamp actuator commands to configured min/max limits, gate updates on validity checks, and emit a compact actuator command bus only when all conditions pass.

jobs.latency_budget: hard real-time; must resolve within the configured timeout window and before command commit
jobs.rationale: The architecture and safety requirements assign freshness, stale-data, and timeout enforcement to deterministic hardware supervision.
jobs.responsibility: Track request sequence numbers, response age, elapsed timeout, and stale-data conditions; reject invalid or late model responses and assert faults as needed.

jobs.latency_budget: immediate on fault detection; no additional cycle beyond detection
jobs.rationale: Safe fallback must remain available independent of model validity, and the architecture explicitly places this in FPGA control supervision.
jobs.responsibility: Drive safe hold or predefined safe actuator state when model data is invalid, stale, missing, or timed out; maintain fault latching until cleared by software.

jobs.latency_budget: offline or nearline; must not delay control loop
jobs.rationale: Traceability and audit logging are richer software tasks and must support the documented acceptance gates and validation evidence.
jobs.responsibility: Record inputs, intermediate states, reference outputs, control outputs, faults, clamp events, stale rejections, and fallback transitions for acceptance-gate evidence.

jobs.rationale: Architecture definition and optimization are explicitly required and are best performed in software before or alongside hardware implementation.
jobs.responsibility: Explore and optimize system structure, interface sizing, timeout settings, fallback policies, and execution partitioning without binding to a specific board or fabric.

tradeoffs: Keeping the surrogate in GPU/CPU software preserves model flexibility and aligns with qualification status, but adds transport latency and service dependency.
Implementing command clamping, freshness checks, and fallback in FPGA improves determinism and safety, but constrains protocol complexity and limits on-device model logic.
Using a compact request/response interface simplifies hardware and I/O budget, but requires disciplined software packaging of geometry descriptors and control context.
CPU reference evaluation maximizes transparency and traceability, but may be slower than a specialized accelerator for large validation sweeps.
A hold-last-good fallback can improve drivability, but must be tightly bounded by safety rules to avoid propagating stale behavior.
Forward compatibility with future GPU/NIM execution is preserved, but the current design cannot claim hardware-surrogate acceleration benefits until the model is qualified for deployment.
